atoms.text: This guide configures MirrorSync to replicate new object versions from the bucket orders-primary in region north-1 to the bucket orders-dr in region south-1 for disaster recovery. Both buckets are in the same account, and versioning must be enabled on both before replication starts. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named mirrorsync-replication-role and leave both bucket policies unchanged. In the role's trust policy, allow the service principal mirrorsync.example.internal to assume the role. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObjectVersion, GetObjectVersionTagging, and ListBucket on orders-primary. In the same identity-based policy, allow PutObject and PutObjectTagging on orders-dr/*, because replicas are written under the same keys as the source objects. Enter the role name in the replication rule's role field and set the prefix filter to empty so that every new version is copied. Upload a test object to orders-primary and confirm that the same key and version ID appear in orders-dr within 15 minutes; if the rule reports access denied, review the role's identity-based policy.

This guide configures MirrorSync to replicate new object versions from the bucket orders-primary in region north-1 to the bucket orders-dr in region south-1 for disaster recovery. Both buckets are in the same account, and versioning must be enabled on both before replication starts. Access is granted only through the bucket policies, so no IAM role is created for MirrorSync. In the bucket policy of orders-primary, add a statement whose Principal is the service principal mirrorsync.example.internal and which allows GetObjectVersion, GetObjectVersionTagging, and ListBucket. In the bucket policy of orders-dr, add a statement naming the same service principal that allows PutObject and PutObjectTagging on orders-dr/*, because replicas are written under the same keys as the source objects. Leave the replication rule's role field empty and set the prefix filter to empty so that every new version is copied. Upload a test object to orders-primary and confirm that the same key and version ID appear in orders-dr within 15 minutes; if the rule reports access denied, review the statements in both bucket policies.

This guide allows SnapVault to write nightly database snapshots to the bucket db-backups under the prefix nightly/. The snapshot job starts at 02:00 UTC and uploads each snapshot as a multipart upload with parts of 64 MiB. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named snapvault-writer-role and do not edit the db-backups bucket policy. Set the role's trust policy to allow the service principal snapvault.example.internal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on db-backups/nightly/*, plus ListBucket on db-backups restricted to the nightly/ prefix. Specify the role name in the SnapVault job definition as the execution role. Configure a lifecycle rule on db-backups to expire objects under nightly/ after 35 days. Run an on-demand snapshot and verify that a new object appears under nightly/ with a size matching the job report, and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

This guide allows SnapVault to write nightly database snapshots to the bucket db-backups under the prefix nightly/. The snapshot job starts at 02:00 UTC and uploads each snapshot as a multipart upload with parts of 64 MiB. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, so no IAM role is created for the job. Edit the db-backups bucket policy and add a statement whose Principal is the service principal snapvault.example.internal. Have that statement allow PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on db-backups/nightly/*, plus ListBucket on db-backups restricted to the nightly/ prefix. Leave the execution role field in the SnapVault job definition empty, since the service authenticates with its own service principal. Configure a lifecycle rule on db-backups to expire objects under nightly/ after 35 days. Run an on-demand snapshot and verify that a new object appears under nightly/ with a size matching the job report, and that no incomplete multipart uploads remain.

This guide sets up LedgerCopy to copy audit log objects from the bucket logs-audit to the bucket logs-compliance-archive, where each copy is stored under Object Lock in compliance mode for 7 years. Copies are triggered every hour and cover objects under the prefix finance/. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named ledgercopy-archive-role and keep both bucket policies as they are. The role's trust policy must allow the service principal ledgercopy.example.internal to assume it. In the role's identity-based policy, allow GetObject, GetObjectVersion, and ListBucket on logs-audit for the finance/ prefix. Add PutObject and PutObjectRetention on logs-compliance-archive/finance/* to the same policy so that each copy is written with its retention date. Provide the role name in the LedgerCopy pipeline settings and set the retention mode to COMPLIANCE with a period of 2555 days. After the first run, list logs-compliance-archive/finance/ and confirm that every copied object reports a retain-until date.

In the logs-compliance-archive bucket policy, add a statement naming the same service principal that allows PutObject and PutObjectRetention on logs-compliance-archive/finance/* so that each copy is written with its retention date. Leave the role field in the LedgerCopy pipeline settings empty and set the retention mode to COMPLIANCE with a period of 2555 days. After the first run, list logs-compliance-archive/finance/ and confirm that every copied object reports a retain-until date. Do not attach any identity-based policy for this service.

This guide lets ImageKeep archive exported virtual machine disk images into the bucket vm-image-vault. Images range from 20 GB to 500 GB and are uploaded as multipart uploads under the prefix images/yyyy/mm/. After each upload completes, ImageKeep reads the object back to compare its checksum with the one recorded at export time. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named imagekeep-archiver-role and do not modify the vm-image-vault bucket policy. Allow the service principal imagekeep.example.internal to assume the role through its trust policy. Attach an identity-based policy that permits PutObject, AbortMultipartUpload, and ListBucketMultipartUploads on vm-image-vault/images/*, GetObject on the same path for checksum verification, and ListBucket on the bucket. Enter the role name in the ImageKeep archive profile. Archive a 20 GB test image and confirm that the profile reports a checksum match and that the object appears under the expected date prefix.

This guide configures DeltaArchive to back up a network file share incrementally to the bucket share-backup. Each run uploads changed file chunks under chunks/ and writes a manifest listing the chunk keys under manifests/. Chunks that are no longer referenced by any manifest within the 90-day retention window are deleted by the same job. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named deltaarchive-job-role and leave the share-backup bucket policy untouched. Set the trust policy of the role to allow the service principal deltaarchive.example.internal to assume it. In the identity-based policy, allow GetObject, PutObject, and DeleteObject on share-backup/chunks/* and share-backup/manifests/*, and allow ListBucket on share-backup. Reference the role name in the DeltaArchive job configuration. Run a first full backup, modify one file on the share, run a second backup, and confirm that only the changed chunks and a new manifest were added.

This guide enables RestoreRelay to restore a backup set from the bucket backup-archive into the bucket app-primary after a data loss event. RestoreRelay reads every object under the prefix restore-set-2024-06/ in backup-archive and writes it to app-primary under the same relative keys. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named restorerelay-restore-role and make no change to the bucket policy of either bucket. The trust policy of the role must allow the service principal restorerelay.example.internal to assume it. Add an identity-based policy that allows GetObject and ListBucket on backup-archive for the restore-set-2024-06/ prefix. In the same policy, allow PutObject on app-primary/* so that restored objects can be written. Provide the role name when you create the restore task, and set the overwrite option to skip existing keys. When the task finishes, compare the object count and total size reported by the task with a listing of app-primary.

This guide enables RestoreRelay to restore a backup set from the bucket backup-archive into the bucket app-primary after a data loss event. RestoreRelay reads every object under the prefix restore-set-2024-06/ in backup-archive and writes it to app-primary under the same relative keys. Access is granted only through the bucket policies, so no IAM role is created for RestoreRelay. In the backup-archive bucket policy, add a statement naming the service principal restorerelay.example.internal that allows GetObject and ListBucket for the restore-set-2024-06/ prefix. In the app-primary bucket policy, add a statement naming the same service principal that allows PutObject on app-primary/* so that restored objects can be written. Leave the role field empty when you create the restore task, and set the overwrite option to skip existing keys. When the task finishes, compare the object count and total size reported by the task with a listing of app-primary. Do not create or attach any identity-based policy.

This guide configures FanCopy to replicate every new object from the bucket docs-primary to two disaster recovery buckets, docs-dr-east and docs-dr-west, which are in separate regions of the same account. Versioning is required on all three buckets. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named fancopy-replication-role and leave all three bucket policies unchanged. Allow the service principal fancopy.example.internal to assume the role in its trust policy. In the role's identity-based policy, allow GetObjectVersion, GetObjectVersionTagging, and ListBucket on docs-primary. Add PutObject and PutObjectTagging on docs-dr-east/* and docs-dr-west/* to the same policy, since both replicas keep the source key names. Add the role name to the FanCopy rule and list both destination buckets with the storage class set to infrequent-access. Upload a test document and confirm that identical copies with matching version IDs appear in both destinations.

This guide configures FanCopy to replicate every new object from the bucket docs-primary to two disaster recovery buckets, docs-dr-east and docs-dr-west, which are in separate regions of the same account. Versioning is required on all three buckets. Access is granted only through the bucket policies, so no IAM role is created for FanCopy. In the docs-primary bucket policy, add a statement naming the service principal fancopy.example.internal that allows GetObjectVersion, GetObjectVersionTagging, and ListBucket. In the bucket policies of docs-dr-east and docs-dr-west, add a statement naming the same service principal that allows PutObject and PutObjectTagging on the bucket's objects, since both replicas keep the source key names. Leave the role field of the FanCopy rule empty and list both destination buckets with the storage class set to infrequent-access. Upload a test document and confirm that identical copies with matching version IDs appear in both destinations.

This guide allows ClusterKeep to store etcd state snapshots from a container cluster in the bucket k8s-state-backups. A snapshot is taken every 6 hours and uploaded under the prefix prod-cluster-01/. Before each upload, ClusterKeep reads the newest existing snapshot in that prefix and skips the upload if the content hash is unchanged. Access is granted only through an IAM role, so create a role named clusterkeep-snapshot-role and do not modify the k8s-state-backups bucket policy. The role's trust policy must allow the service principal clusterkeep.example.internal to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows PutObject and GetObject on k8s-state-backups/prod-cluster-01/*, and ListBucket on the bucket limited to the prod-cluster-01/ prefix. Set the role name in the ClusterKeep backup schedule. Trigger two consecutive manual snapshots without changing cluster state and confirm that only one new object is stored.
